record.paper_title: Recent results on functional equations in a single variable, perspectives and open problems
record.original_question: Find all continuous self-mappings φ:(0,∞)→(0,∞) that satisfy the functional equation φ(x f(φ(x))) = g(φ(x)), where f and g are the given functions appearing in equation (3.10). The paper states that this problem was posed in full generality after special power-function cases had been studied.

evidence.quote: This is the case, for instance, with the equation ϕ(xf(ϕ(x))) = g(ϕ(x)) (3.10) studied for power functions f and g by P. Kahlig, A. Matkowska and J. Matkowski in [132]. In general case, J. Matkowski (oral communication) posed the problem to find all continuous self-mappings of (0,∞) satisfying (3.10).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $f,g:(0,\infty)\to(0,\infty)$ be given continuous functions. Determine all continuous self-mappings $\varphi:(0,\infty)\to(0,\infty)$ satisfying the functional equation
$$\varphi\bigl(x\,f(\varphi(x))\bigr) \;=\; g(\varphi(x)) \qquad \text{for all } x\in(0,\infty).$$
The case where $f$ and $g$ are power functions (i.e. $f(t)=t^{a}$, $g(t)=t^{b}$ for some real exponents $a,b$) has been treated; the problem is to solve the equation for general continuous $f$ and $g$.
artifact.category_tag: Functional equations in a single variable
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches did not locate a complete solution for the general continuous-function case. Only the special case of power functions f and g appears to have been treated in the literature (Kahlig–Matkowska–Matkowski). The problem of describing all continuous self-mappings of (0,∞) satisfying the equation for general continuous f and g appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: On the Composition of Homogeneous Quasi-Arithmetic Means (Kahlig–Matkowski)
status_evidence.snippet: Work by Kahlig and Matkowski on related functional equations involving power-type compositions.
status_evidence.claim: Only special (power-function) cases of related equations are documented; general continuous case not found resolved.

status_evidence.title: Regular solutions of a functional equation derived from the invariance problem of Matkowski means
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work on invariance functional equations of Matkowski type.
status_evidence.claim: Recent activity exists on related Matkowski-type functional equations, but the specific general-case problem is not reported as solved.
